Random effects of a parameter transformation

Source: R/randomEffects.R
randomEffects.Rd

Returns the random-effect structure that insert() with effect formulas attached to a branched transformation: the random terms, their groupings, distributions and correlation blocks, and the parameters the formulas created. em() takes it as random and builds the prior of the random effects from it. P() keeps the structure, so randomEffects() takes the transformation or the parameter function built from it.

An effect formula cl ~ wt + (1 + dose | p | ID) replaces the symbol cl wherever it occurs in a branch by a linear predictor. The scale of the symbol is the one the transformation gives it: after insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = "cl") the random effects are normal on the log scale. The parts of an effect formula:

left-hand side

one or more symbols of the transformation, ka + v ~ ... applies the right-hand side to each.

fixed effects

the terms outside the bars, coded as by stats::model.matrix() (treatment contrasts) over the columns of the branch table. The intercept keeps the name of the symbol (cl), the other columns are cl_<column> (cl_wt, cl_log_wt).

random terms

(1 | ID), (1 + dose | ID) with a random slope, (1 | p | ID) with an ID p: terms with the same ID and grouping are correlated across formulas, the columns of one term are correlated, other terms are independent. gr(ID, dist = spikeSlab()) instead of ID sets the distribution, see normal(). The random effect of a group is eta_<symbol>_<group> for the intercept and eta_<symbol>_<column>_<group> for a slope; a symbol with random terms in a second grouping gets the grouping name in the stem, eta_cl_center_<group>.

Usage

randomEffects(trafo)

# S3 method for class 'randomeffects'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

trafo

A branched transformation from insert() with effect formulas, or a parameter function P() built from one.

x

A randomeffects object.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class randomeffects, a list with terms (one row per random effect column: symbol, origin (the formula), term, column, group, id, dist, the fixed hyperparameters prob, concentration and tau (NA where estimated) and stem, the name stem of the etas), blocks (groups of rows: the normal rows of a block are correlated, the rows of a spike-and-slab or Dirichlet-process block share the hyperparameters), subjects (the groups of each grouping and the conditions they own), fixed (the parameters the formulas created), etas (eta names, one row per condition, one column per term row), groups (per stem the group of each condition), fixedDesign (per symbol the model matrix of the fixed effects, one row per condition) and etaNames (NULL for random effects from insert()).

See also

insert(), em(), normal()

Examples

## Log parameters; clearance with a weight covariate and a random intercept and dose
## slope per subject, correlated with the random intercept of the absorption rate
cov <- data.frame(ID = c("s1", "s2", "s3"), wt = c(62, 75, 81), dose = c(100, 100, 200),
                  row.names = c("C1", "C2", "C3"))
trafo <- branch(define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("ka", "cl", "v")), table = cov)
trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = c("ka", "cl", "v"))
trafo <- insert(trafo,
                ka ~ 1 + (1 | p | ID),
                cl ~ wt + (1 + dose | p | ID),
                v  ~ 1 + (1 | gr(ID, dist = spikeSlab())))
trafo$C2
#> Idx Inner <- Outer
#>   1    cl <- exp((cl+cl_wt*75+eta_cl_s2+eta_cl_dose_s2*100))
#>   2    ka <- exp((ka+eta_ka_s2))
#>   3     v <- exp((v+eta_v_s2))
re <- randomEffects(trafo)
re
#> Random effects: 4 terms over ID
#>   block 1 (normal, ID): eta_ka, eta_cl, eta_cl_dose
#>   block 2 (spikeSlab, prob estimated, tau estimated, ID): eta_v
#>   fixed effects: ka, cl, cl_wt, v 
re$fixed
#> [1] "ka"    "cl"    "cl_wt" "v"    

## One random intercept for many parameters at once
randomEffects(insert(branch(define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("ka", "cl", "v")), table = cov),
                     x ~ 1 + (1 | ID), x = c("ka", "cl", "v")))
#> Random effects: 3 terms over ID
#>   block 1 (normal, ID): eta_ka
#>   block 2 (normal, ID): eta_cl
#>   block 3 (normal, ID): eta_v
#>   fixed effects: ka, cl, v
